text: Clean code is writing that is easy for others—and your future self—to understand. One important aspect is using clear naming conventions: variable and function names should describe exactly what they do, like `calculateTotal` instead of `doStuff`. Breaking your program into small, focused functions also helps. Each function should have a single purpose, making the code easier to test and reuse. This approach greatly improves maintainability because when code is readable and logically organized, you can quickly find and fix issues or add new features. In short, writing clean code saves time and reduces stress for everyone who works with it.
